cards.title: Why sequences need memory
cards.hook: One frame tells you where; several frames tell you where it's going.
cards.visual:
StructureExample
one-to-oneimage classification
many-to-onesentiment of a review; ECG → diagnosis
one-to-manyimage captioning; seed → music
many-to-manytranslation; speech → text
formula: preserve order, carry context, share parameters, variable length
example: 'Mando protects Grogu' vs 'Grogu protects Mando': same words, different meaning.
cards.trap: Applying the same network to each step independently does NOT pass information between steps.

cards.title: The RNN hidden-state update
cards.src: Lecture 8, slide 20-29; Key points about a simple RNN hidden-state update
cards.hook: New memory = squash(current input + old memory).
cards.visual:
QuantityKey-points example
xₜ, wₓ2, 0.5 → 1.0
hₜ₋₁, wₕ0.4, 0.25 → 0.1
sum (no bias)1.1
tanh(1.1) lookup0.800 = hₜ
example: Same cell and same W_xh, W_hh, W_hy at every step; only xₜ, hₜ, ŷₜ change.
cards.memory: Input × input-weight, memory × recurrent-weight, add, squash.
cards.trap: The sum before activation is NOT the new hidden state. Add a bias only if specified.

cards.title: Training RNNs: BPTT and vanishing gradients
cards.hook: Gradients flowing back through many steps get multiplied again and again.
cards.visual:
Repeated factorEffectFix
> 1explodinggradient clipping
< 1 (0.8³⁰ ≈ 0.001)vanishing → short-term biasactivation, init, architecture (LSTM/GRU)
formula: sum losses → backprop once → update shared params
cards.trap: Gradient clipping fixes EXPLODING, not vanishing gradients.

cards.title: Naive Bayes sentiment
cards.hook: Multiply the prior by how typical each word is of each class.
cards.memory: Naive = pretend words don't affect each other.
cards.trap: Without smoothing a zero count wipes out the whole product.

cards.title: N-grams and Word2Vec
cards.hook: Count what comes next, or learn vectors where similar words live together.
formula: h = average of context embeddings; predict centre
centre embedding predicts each context word
example: v(Paris) − v(France) + v(Italy) ≈ v(Rome) (cosine 0.707); v(Uncle) − v(Man) + v(Woman) ≈ v(Aunt) (0.824).
cards.trap: N-grams have a fixed context and no notion that 'Grogu ≈ foundling'.
